summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests ipilimumab and nivolumab together with cryoablation, a procedure that freezes part of a tumor, in adults with advanced melanoma that is growing or resistant after prior immunotherapy. Ipilimumab and nivolumab are given by intravenous infusion for cycles 1 to 4 at pre-determined doses under the oncologist's direction, and a core needle biopsy followed by cryoablation is done between cycles 1 and 2. The record does not state a main outcome measure, but it says the study aims to assess safety and effectiveness, and Stage 1 moves to Stage 2 if 6 or more of 15 participants have clinical benefit.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ipilimumab y nivolumab junto con crioablación, un procedimiento que congela parte de un tumor, en adultos con melanoma avanzado que crece o es resistente después de una inmunoterapia previa. El ipilimumab y el nivolumab se administran por infusión intravenosa en los ciclos 1 a 4, con dosis predeterminadas y bajo la dirección del oncólogo, y se realiza una biopsia con aguja gruesa seguida de crioablación entre los ciclos 1 y 2. El registro no indica una medida principal de resultado, pero señala que el estudio busca evaluar la seguridad y la eficacia, y que la Etapa 1 pasa a la Etapa 2 si 6 o más de 15 participantes presentan beneficio clínico.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with unresectable melanoma that progressed on prior immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
Treating physician plans to start ipilimumab and nivolumab together.
Tumor suitable for percutaneous image-guided cryoablation under routine interventional radiology criteria.
Measurable disease by RECIST, apart from the lesion to be ablated.
ECOG performance status 2 or less, with adequate blood counts and organ function.
not_for: Progressing on ipilimumab and nivolumab as the last line of therapy.
Unresolved side effects above grade 1 from prior cancer treatment, or ongoing immune-related adverse events.
Symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease.
Prednisone above 10 mg daily or equivalent, or uncontrolled illness.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or currently receiving an investigational agent.
